summary: @servicetitan/responsive preinstall downloads Bun runtime and executes bundled obfuscated payload
details: The package advertises itself as a React responsive-components library, but its package.json declares a preinstall hook ("node setup.mjs") that runs automatically on npm install. setup.mjs downloads the Bun runtime from github.com/oven-sh/bun releases, extracts it to a temp directory, chmods it executable, and uses it to execute a bundled 727 KB file named math_init.js. math_init.js is a heavily obfuscated @bun-cjs bundle using obfuscator.io-style patterns (hex-named variables such as MmgoCP/etDiOOB, a rotated string-array, and a WV8StW rotator function). Executing an obfuscated payload of this size via a smuggled alternate language runtime at install time is inconsistent with the package's declared purpose as a responsive UI component library, and bypasses tooling that inspects only Node-resolved code paths. The alternate-runtime dropper pattern, the file naming (math_init) that does not match the responsive-UI advertised function, and the scale of obfuscation are characteristic of a supply-chain payload rather than a build helper.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
